en.title: Pair Sum Queries
en.description:
Given integer arrays a and b, process two types of queries in order: `0 i x` increases a[i] by x, where i is a 0-based index; `1 x` asks for the number of index pairs (i,j) such that a[i]+b[j]=x. Different positions are counted separately.

Parts of the input protocol and constraints marked "site supplement" were compiled by this site and are not additional conditions of the original problem.
en.input: The first line contains n m q. The second line contains the n integers of a, the third line contains the m integers of b, and the next q lines are queries. Site-supplemented ranges: 1≤n,m≤200000, 1≤q≤200000; initial values, increments, and targets have absolute value ≤10^9, and every updated a[i] is guaranteed to have absolute value ≤10^12; it is also guaranteed that over all type 1 queries, Σ min(Da,Db)≤10^7, where Da and Db are the numbers of distinct values in a and b at the time of that query. This limit corresponds to the program iterating over the smaller frequency table on each query.
en.output: For each `1 x` query, output the corresponding number of index pairs in order, separated by spaces; if there are no such queries, output an empty line.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the rules above; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
